title: Governed Harness Monkey Testing
subtitle: Seeded perturbation for contract and concept hardening
scope: Seeded monkey-test pattern for living-doc harness contracts, lifecycle routing, artifact references, and concept-level invariants.
sourceCoverage: Session-derived objective shaped from the harness chaining proof work, existing contract suite surfaces, and the desired monkey-test pattern.
objective: Create a governed monkey-test pattern for the living-doc harness that uses seeded, bounded perturbations to stress inference-unit contracts, artifact references, routing policy, lifecycle gate states, and concept-level invariants. The pattern must expose under-tested assumptions without creating flaky CI: every generated case must be reproducible from a seed, checked against named harness invariants, able to emit replay artifacts on failure, and connected back to the concept or contract it hardens.
successCondition: The objective is met only when the harness has a CI-safe seeded monkey-test surface that can generate bounded valid and invalid lifecycle cases, reject contract and routing violations deterministically, write replay artifacts for failures, map each generated case to a named concept or invariant, and promote any failure into a normal deterministic regression test. Random noise, unreplayable fuzzing, report-only output, or tests that merely exercise happy-path examples cannot satisfy closure.

objectiveFacets.label: Seeded replayable generation
objectiveFacets.description: Every monkey run is deterministic from an explicit seed and can be replayed from saved artifacts.

objectiveFacets.label: Bounded perturbation surface
objectiveFacets.description: Mutations are limited to approved harness inputs such as contracts, artifact references, route recommendations, gate states, timestamps, iteration ids, allowed unit sets, and fixture evidence.

objectiveFacets.label: Contract and lifecycle invariants
objectiveFacets.description: Generated cases are judged by named invariants, not by random execution success.

objectiveFacets.label: Concept hardening
objectiveFacets.description: Each case explains which system concept it pressures, such as controller-owned routing, artifact-ref continuity, side-effect gates, closure authority, or evidence freshness.

objectiveFacets.label: CI-safe monkey pattern
objectiveFacets.description: The default suite is deterministic, bounded, offline, and timeout-limited so it strengthens CI without introducing flaky behavior.

invariants.statement: No monkey failure counts as actionable unless the seed, generated case, mutation list, expected invariant, actual result, and replay command are saved.
The monkey runner must not mutate arbitrary files, call real network services, invoke real Codex execution, or perform external side effects in the default contract path.
A monkey pass proves only that named invariants survived the generated cases; it does not replace maximal-chain proof, production replay, or objective closure review.
A concept is not hardened until at least one generated case fails if that concept's rule is broken.

sections.title: Acceptance Criteria
sections.summary: Closure gates for a governed monkey-test pattern.

data.title: Seeded harness monkey runner
data.criterion: A harness monkey test runner exists for seeded runs and reproduces the same generated cases from the same seed.
data.proofRequired: A command such as `node tests/contract/living-doc-harness-monkey.spec.mjs --seed <seed>` or an equivalent npm script executes deterministic generated cases.
data.acceptanceTest: Running the same seed twice produces the same case ids, mutation list, expected invariants, and pass/fail results.
data.proofObserved: npm run test:harness-monkey passes with seed 20260514 and 48 deterministic generated cases.

data.title: Approved mutation surfaces only
data.criterion: Monkey cases are limited to approved harness surfaces and cannot mutate arbitrary repository files or execute external side effects.
data.proofRequired: The generator declares its mutation domains and tests reject mutation requests outside those domains.
data.acceptanceTest: Attempts to mutate arbitrary files, network behavior, real Codex execution, or non-fixture source files are rejected before case execution.
data.proofObserved: The generated report touches only inference-unit-output, artifact-ref, routing-policy, lifecycle-gates, and evidence-freshness surfaces.

data.title: Contract violations rejected deterministically
data.objectiveTerm: inference-unit contracts, artifact references, routing policy
data.criterion: Generated invalid contracts are rejected deterministically with precise reason codes.
data.proofRequired: Monkey cases cover invalid transitions, missing artifact references, malformed references, stale iteration references, disallowed unit types, and mismatched evidence.
data.acceptanceTest: The suite fails if any generated invalid contract is accepted by routing, artifact-ref validation, or lifecycle finalization.
data.proofObserved: Generated cases reject invalid output contracts, invalid transitions, disallowed unit selections, malformed artifact refs, stale/escaping refs, and mismatched routing expectations.

data.title: Lifecycle invariants survive generated chains
data.objectiveTerm: lifecycle gate states and concept-level invariants
data.criterion: Randomized valid and invalid lifecycle chains preserve the core lifecycle authority rules.
data.proofRequired: Generated chains assert that reviewer output cannot directly close terminal state, closure-review remains required, commit evidence gates source changes, PR-review gates configured PR policy, and same-reason continuation cannot loop indefinitely.
data.acceptanceTest: The suite fails if a generated chain bypasses closure-review, skips a required side-effect gate, accepts stale evidence, or repeats the same unresolved continuation reason beyond the configured bound.
data.proofObserved: Generated routing and closure-authority cases preserve closure-review authority, commit/PR gates, continuation loop blocking, and latest-evidence route selection.

data.title: Failure output is replayable
data.objectiveTerm: able to emit replay artifacts on failure
data.criterion: Any failing generated case writes a replay artifact that is sufficient to rerun or inspect the exact failure.
data.proofRequired: Failure artifacts include seed, case id, generated chain, mutation list, expected invariant, actual result, reason codes, artifact paths, and minimal reproduction command.
data.acceptanceTest: A saved replay artifact can drive the same failure without relying on the original random generator state.
data.proofObserved: The contract spec intentionally runs a tampered case with throwOnFailure false and verifies the emitted living-doc-harness-monkey-replay/v1 artifact shape.

data.title: Cases map to hardened concepts
data.objectiveTerm: connected back to the concept or contract it hardens
data.criterion: Every generated case declares which named concept, invariant, or contract rule it pressures.
data.proofRequired: Runner output or report JSON lists concept ids for each case.
data.acceptanceTest: The suite fails if a generated case has no concept or invariant mapping.
data.proofObserved: Every generated case declares concept ids, and the report summary touches controller-owned-routing, artifact-ref-continuity, closure-authority, evidence-freshness, and side-effect-gates.

data.title: CI-safe default run
data.criterion: The default monkey test configuration is deterministic, bounded, offline, and timeout-limited.
data.proofRequired: The default command uses a fixed seed set, bounded case count, deterministic timeout, and no real network or Codex dependency.
data.acceptanceTest: The test suite remains stable under repeated local runs and in `npm run test:contract` if added to the contract path.
data.proofObserved: The monkey spec is in npm run test:contract; the full contract suite passed locally after adding the runner.

data.title: Failures promote to normal regressions
data.criterion: A failing monkey case can be promoted into a fixed deterministic fixture or named contract test.
data.proofRequired: A replay artifact schema and fixture-loading path exist.
data.acceptanceTest: At least one seeded replay fixture is exercised as a named deterministic regression test.
data.proofObserved: Replay artifacts can rerun a failing generated case, but no real monkey-discovered production failure has been promoted into a permanent fixture yet.

data.title: Report shows what was hardened
data.criterion: The monkey output reports seed, case count, generated cases, pass/fail invariants, concepts touched, and replay artifact paths.
data.proofRequired: Generated JSON and, if useful, HTML report output exists for the monkey run.
data.acceptanceTest: A reviewer can identify which concepts were stressed and which invariant would have failed from the report alone.
data.proofObserved: docs/living-doc-harness-monkey-test-report.json lists seed, case count, cases, results, mutation surfaces, concepts touched, and replay artifact paths.

sections.title: Mutation Boundaries
sections.summary: Allowed surfaces for monkey perturbation. Anything outside this list is out of scope for the default CI-safe runner.

data.title: Inference-unit output contracts
mustReject: unit recommendations disallowed by the transition matrix

data.title: Artifact references
mustReject: loose run-local paths where artifact refs are required
references that resolve outside the run evidence boundary
references that do not match the expected unit or iteration

data.title: Routing policy and allowed unit set
mustReject: route recommendations not accepted by the controller
hard-coded sequences that bypass the matrix policy table

data.title: Lifecycle gate states
allowedMutations: PR-review required, missing, approved, or blocked
mustReject: closure while required commit evidence is missing
closure while required PR-review evidence is missing or blocked

data.title: Evidence freshness
mustReject: newer valid unit recommendation overridden by stale blocker facts
evidence from a different iteration treated as current
same-reason continuation accepted against unchanged evidence

sections.title: Concept Hardening Map
sections.summary: Concepts that must become executable invariants rather than explanatory language.

data.title: Controller-owned routing
data.claim: Inference units emit typed claims and recommendations; the lifecycle controller validates and selects the next unit.
data.failureQuestion: Can a generated case make a unit directly authorize the next lifecycle step without controller validation?
data.expectedFailureMode: The route is rejected with a contract-visible reason code.

data.title: Artifact-ref continuity
data.claim: Cross-unit handoffs must use resolvable artifact references that preserve run, unit, iteration, and artifact identity.
data.failureQuestion: Can a generated case replace a required artifact ref with a loose path, stale ref, or mismatched unit artifact?
data.expectedFailureMode: The handoff is rejected before the next unit consumes it.

data.title: Closure authority
data.claim: Reviewer closure claims are not terminal authority; closure-review approval plus controller persistence is required.
data.failureQuestion: Can a generated case close terminal state directly from reviewer output?
data.expectedFailureMode: Terminal closure is blocked and rerouted or marked continuation-required.

data.title: Evidence freshness
data.claim: Latest valid unit evidence must control route selection over stale blocker facts or unchanged continuation reasons.
data.failureQuestion: Can a generated case let stale evidence override newer valid route authority?
data.expectedFailureMode: The stale evidence is rejected or recorded as a blocker instead of silently driving the route.

data.title: Governed monkey control loop
data.claim: Monkey testing is useful only when the random generator is subordinate to deterministic contracts, invariant oracles, and replay artifacts.
data.validationQuestion: Does every generated case have a seed, bounded mutation surface, invariant oracle, concept mapping, and replay path?

diagrams.title: Governed monkey pattern
diagrams.text:
flowchart LR
  Seed[seed and fixed config] --> Gen[bounded case generator]
  Gen --> Case[generated lifecycle or contract case]
  Case --> Oracle[named invariant oracle]
  Oracle --> Pass[pass with concept coverage]
  Oracle --> Fail[failure with reason code]
  Fail --> Replay[replay artifact]
  Replay --> Regression[promoted deterministic regression]
  Concepts[concept map] -. labels cases .-> Case
  Bounds[mutation boundaries] -. constrain generator .-> Gen

sections.title: Proof Ladder
sections.summary: The proof should move from example-based contract coverage to seeded generated pressure with replayable failures.

data.title: Existing contract suite
notes: `npm run test:contract` already covers many deterministic harness contracts and lifecycle edges.
This is the base layer the monkey pattern must not weaken.
data.nextStrongerProof: Seeded generated cases that stress the same contracts with varied states and invalid combinations.

data.title: Seeded monkey generator
notes: A default fixed seed set and bounded case count should be enough for CI.
A developer mode may allow ad hoc seeds without changing CI behavior.

data.title: Replay artifact path
notes: Failures must write enough structure to reproduce the case deterministically.
Replay artifacts should become fixtures when they reveal a real system gap.
data.nextStrongerProof: Promoted regression cases that stay in the normal contract suite.

data.title: Concept coverage
notes: The report should show which concepts were pressured by each generated case.
A concept with no failing mutation pressure remains explanatory, not hardened.
The current report shows concept coverage; permanent regression promotion remains the next stronger proof after a real generated failure.
data.nextStrongerProof: A stable concept coverage report that shows hardened concepts and known gaps.

sections.title: Out Of Scope
sections.summary: Boundaries that keep the first monkey pattern useful rather than noisy.

data.title: No pure random fuzzing
data.decision: The first version must be seeded, bounded, and replayable.
data.rationale: Unreplayable failures do not harden the harness because they cannot become regression tests.

data.title: No real Codex or network dependency
data.decision: The default monkey suite must use mocks, fixtures, or fake headless surfaces only.
data.rationale: The objective is CI-safe contract hardening, not production execution proof.

data.title: No load or performance stress testing
data.decision: Performance stress, concurrency load, and long-running soak tests are outside this objective.
data.rationale: The first target is contract and concept validity under varied generated states.

data.title: Monkey pass does not equal harness closure
data.decision: A monkey-test pass cannot replace maximal-chain proof, production replay, or objective closure review.
data.rationale: The pattern is a pressure tool for assumptions, not a universal proof of the harness.
